items.prompt: In a B-tree of order 5, what is the most keys a node can hold?
hints: The order is the most children a node may have.
A node with m children holds m − 1 keys.
Order 5 → at most 5 children → at most 4 keys.

options.feedback: 5 is the most children. Keys sit between children, so there is one fewer.
2 is the fewest keys a non-root node may hold, not the most.

items.prompt: In a B-tree of order 5, what is the fewest keys a node other than the root can hold?
hints: The minimum is about half the maximum.
Every node except the root holds at least ⌈m/2⌉ − 1 keys.

options.feedback: 3 = ⌈5/2⌉ is the fewest children for an internal node. Subtract one for keys.
Only the root may drop to a single key in an order-5 tree.

items.prompt: Is this a valid order-3 B-tree?
hints: Count the keys in each node.
An order-3 node holds at most 2 keys.

items.prompt: Is this a valid order-5 B-tree?
hints: Check the smallest node that is not the root.
In order 5, every node except the root needs at least 2 keys.

items.prompt: Is this a valid order-3 B-tree?
hints: Check each key against the keys above it.
Keys in the left subtree of 20 must be smaller than 20.
25 sits left of 20 but is larger than 20.

items.prompt: Is this a valid order-3 B-tree?
hints: Check each rule in turn: key counts, children, order, leaf level.
Each node has 1 or 2 keys, and the root has one more child than keys.
All rules hold: every leaf is on level 2 and every key is in the right range.
